chipOpen: Remember me on all my phones
title: Remember me on all my phones (optional)
intro: Turn on a passkey and your orders, name and saved address follow you to a new phone.
adv1: Your orders are still there after a new phone or cleared browser
adv2: Your name and saved address are filled in for you
adv3: Sellers see the same customer code every time (and know it is really you)
why1: No email, no password, no phone number
why2: It unlocks with your face or fingerprint
why3: Your saved address is sealed so only your phones can read it (not even we can)
why4: It is deleted if you don't order for 30 days, and you can delete it any time
note: Ordering without it works just the same.
passkeyP: A safer way to sign in, built into your phone. Instead of a password, you unlock with your face, fingerprint or phone PIN, the same way you unlock your phone. It's stored safely on your phone (and your phone's backup), and it only works for this app.
noPrf: This phone can't seal your address. Your orders and name will follow you, but your saved address stays on this phone only.
already: I already use Remember me (e.g. in another kitchen's app)
errCancelled: Nothing was changed. You can try again any time.
errFailed: That did not work. Please try again.
errOtherKind: That's a seller passkey. Choose your Remember me passkey.
errExists: This phone already has a Remember me passkey. Choose “I already use Remember me”.
errBadCode: That code is not right or has expired.
errBadCodeTries: That code is not right or has expired. {{count}} tries left.
errLocked: Too many tries. Please wait a few minutes.
errUnsupported: This browser can't use a passkey here. Open the app from your home screen or use Safari or Chrome.
cardOffP: Optional. Your orders, name and saved address follow you to a new phone. No email, no password.
codeHere: Your customer code at this kitchen
codeHint: Each kitchen sees a different code. It is not linked to your name or phone.
sealedOn: Your saved address is sealed with your passkey.
signOutAsk: This phone stops using Remember me. Your saved data stays; turn it back on any time with your passkey.
delNote: Deletes your orders list, name and sealed address from our servers. Orders already placed stay with the kitchen until it clears them.
delAsk: Everything on our side is deleted at once. This phone keeps its own My orders. This cannot be undone.
removeSignalled: We also told your phone the passkey is no longer valid.
removeByHand: To remove the passkey from your phone too: iPhone: Settings > Passwords. Android: Google Password Manager. A leftover passkey does nothing without our data.
setupP: This phone is added. Add its own passkey so it stays signed in.
apP: On the new phone choose “Restore” and type this code.
joinP: On a phone where you are already signed in, open Settings > Remember me > Add another phone and type the 6 digit code it shows.
restoreQ: Had orders on another phone or app?
restored_one: {{count}} order restored. Your name and customer codes are back too.
restored_other: {{count}} orders restored. Your name and customer codes are back too.
restoredNone: Signed in. Your name and customer codes are back.
pushAgain: Turn on order updates on this phone too
nudge: Remember me on all your phones?
privacyOpen: How we keep your data private
privacyTitle: How we keep your data private
rm1: If you turn it on, we keep a random id, your passkey's public key, your first name and the list of your order links (which kitchen each belongs to). No email, no password, no phone number.
rm2: Your saved delivery address is sealed with your passkey, so only your phones can read it, not even we can. It is deleted when you haven't ordered for 30 days.
rm3: Each kitchen sees a different customer code for you. It is not linked to your name or phone, and kitchens never see your id.
rm4: A Remember me that has not been used for 12 months is deleted automatically.
rm5: Turn it off any time: Settings > Remember me > Delete my saved data removes everything on our side at once. Your phone keeps its own My orders.
rm6: To remove the passkey from your phone by hand: iPhone: Settings > Passwords. Android: Google Password Manager. A leftover passkey is useless once our data is deleted.
passkeyMore: A passkey is a safer way to sign in that is built into your phone: you unlock with your face, fingerprint or phone PIN instead of a password. It only works for this app.
